extracted.intended_audience: persons and entities (including non‑U.S. citizens), counsel, and stakeholders who prepare and submit citizen petitions to the FDA / Dockets Management Staff
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and procedural requirements for preparing, filing, and managing citizen petitions to the Commissioner of Food and Drugs under 21 CFR 10.30, including required petition contents, submission methods, docketing, agency response timing, and record rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of section
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies to any petition submitted by a person (including a person who is not a citizen of the United States) except to the extent that other sections of this chapter apply different requirements to a particular matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies who may use the citizen petition process and notes that other chapter sections may impose different requirements for particular matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: General submission compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition (including any attachments) must be submitted in accordance with § 10.20 and, if applicable, § 10.31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All petitions and attachments must follow formatting and submission rules in §10.20; if §10.31 certification applies, follow that section instead of the certification requirement in §10.30(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission option and requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions (including any attachments) may be electronically submitted in accordance with paragraph (b)(3) of this section and § 10.20 through http://www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one electronic copy is necessary. When submitting electronically, follow the petition format requirements in paragraph (b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail or non-electronic submission address and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition (including any attachments) not electronically submitted must be submitted in accordance with paragraph (b)(3) and § 10.20 and delivered to Dockets Management Staff, FDA, 5630 Fishers Lane, Rm. 1061, Rockville, MD 20852.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit two copies (original and redacted version) for confidential petitions; otherwise one copy is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required petition format (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition submitted under paragraphs (b)(1) or (b)(2) must be in accordance with § 10.20 and in the following format: 'Citizen Petition Date: The undersigned submits this petition under ____ (relevant statutory sections, if known) ... to request the Commissioner of Food and Drugs to____ (issue, amend, or revoke a regulation or order or take or refrain from taking any other form of administrative action).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed header and include the statutory basis and the specific administrative action requested; follow §10.20 formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Requested (required content)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition requests the Commissioner to issue, amend, or revoke a regulation, provide the exact wording of the existing regulation (if any) and the proposed regulation or amendment requested; if requesting an order, provide the exact wording of the citation to the existing order (if any) and the exact wording requested for the proposed order; if requesting other administrative action, state the specific action or relief requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise: include exact current and proposed regulatory or order language or clearly state the specific relief sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Grounds (required content and completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A full statement, in a well-organized format, of the factual and legal grounds on which the petitioner relies, including all relevant information and views on which the petitioner relies, as well as representative information known to the petitioner which is unfavorable to the petitioner's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a comprehensive, well-organized factual and legal argument and disclose adverse information known to the petitioner; omission of unfavorable representative data is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Impact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include either a claim for categorical exclusion under §§ 25.30, 25.31, 25.32, 25.33, or § 25.34 of this chapter or an environmental assessment under § 25.40 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clearly whether the action is categorically excluded or submit the required environmental assessment per the cited provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic Impact (when requested)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit economic information only when requested by the Commissioner: a statement of the effect of requested action on (1) cost (and price) increases to industry, government, and consumers; (2) productivity of wage earners, businesses, or government; (3) competition; (4) supplies of important materials, products, or services; (5) employment; and (6) energy supply or demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include economic impact material unless the Commissioner requests it; if requested, respond on each enumerated factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification by petitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: The undersigned certifies that, to the best knowledge and belief of the undersigned, this petition includes all information and views on which the petition relies, and that it includes representative data and information known to the petitioner which are unfavorable to the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include signature, name, mailing address, and telephone number. Note that petitions subject to §10.31's certification requirement are exempt from this certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing, docketing, and unique docket number
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition that appears to meet the requirements will be filed by the Dockets Management Staff, stamped with the date of filing, and assigned a unique docket number which identifies the docket file for all submissions relating to the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent submissions must refer to the assigned docket number; related petitions may be filed together and given the same docket number; Dockets Management Staff will promptly notify the petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment on filed petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested person may submit comments to the Dockets Management Staff on a filed petition, which comments become part of the docket file; comments must specify the docket number and include, if applicable, the verification under § 10.31, and may support or oppose the petition in whole or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for alternative or different administrative action must be submitted as a separate petition (i.e., comments cannot function as a separate petition requesting different action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's considerations in ruling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall, in accordance with paragraph (e)(2), rule upon each petition filed, taking into consideration (i) available agency resources for the category of subject matter, (ii) the priority assigned to the petition considering both the category of subject matter involved and the overall work of the agency, and (iii) time requirements established by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition priority and available resources affect the Commissioner's timeliness and handling; statutory deadlines also constrain action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard response timeline and possible response types
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraphs (e)(4) and (5), the Commissioner shall furnish a response to each petitioner within 180 days of receipt. The response will either: (i) approve the petition (and concurrently take appropriate action), (ii) deny the petition, (iii) dismiss the petition if it is rendered moot, or (iv) provide a tentative response indicating why the agency has been unable to reach a decision and possibly indicating the likely ultimate response and when a final response may be furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tentative response may cite agency priorities or need for additional information; approved petitions trigger appropriate implementation (e.g., Federal Register notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special expedited response rules (505(j)(2)(C) and 505(q))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall furnish a response within 90 days for petitions filed under section 505(j)(2)(C) (response will either approve or disapprove) and intends to furnish a response within 150 days for petitions subject to section 505(q). Agency action on a 505(j)(2)(C) petition is governed by § 314.93.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different statutory provisions impose shorter response deadlines and may constrain available response options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of other procedural sections when requesting regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition requests the Commissioner to issue, amend, or revoke a regulation, § 10.40 or § 10.50 also apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory rulemaking provisions and procedures (e.g., notice-and-comment or other rulemaking processes) will be triggered where a regulation is at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementing, amending, or withdrawing petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may supplement, amend, or withdraw a petition without Agency approval and without prejudice to resubmission at any time until the Commissioner rules on the petition, unless the petition has been referred for a hearing under parts 12–15. After a ruling or referral, a petition may be supplemented, amended, or withdrawn only with the approval of the Commissioner. The Commissioner may approve withdrawal, with or without prejudice against resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes are unrestricted before Commissioner action unless a hearing referral has occurred; after action/referral, changes require Agency approval and withdrawal may carry prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures available to the Commissioner in review
rubrics_metrics.description: In reviewing a petition the Commissioner may use conferences, meetings, discussions, and correspondence under § 10.65; a hearing under parts 12–16; a Federal Register notice requesting information and views; a proposal to issue, amend, or revoke a regulation in accordance with § 10.40 or § 12.20; or any other specific public procedure established in this chapter and expressly applicable to the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency may choose one or more procedural avenues (informal conferences, formal hearings, notice-and-comment, etc.) as appropriate to the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the administrative record
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the administrative proceeding consists of: (1) the petition including all information on which it relies; (2) all comments received on the petition; (3) if the petition resulted in a proposal to issue, amend, or revoke a regulation, all documents specified in § 10.40(g); (4) documents resulting from optional procedures under paragraph (h) (except closed transcripts); (5) the Commissioner's decision and supporting information filed with Dockets Management Staff; (6) all documents filed under § 10.65(h); and (7) if a petition for reconsideration or for a stay is filed under paragraph (j), the administrative record specified in § 10.33(k) or § 10.35(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is exhaustive for purposes of the administrative record; closed portions of advisory committee transcripts are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusivity and closure of administrative record
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative record specified is the exclusive record for the Commissioner's decision. The record closes on the date of the Commissioner's decision unless some other date is specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person wishing to rely upon information not included in the administrative record must submit it in a new petition to modify the decision (e.g., a petition for reconsideration or stay under §10.33 or §10.35).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions: referral and routine correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: This section does not apply to referral of a matter to a United States attorney for initiation of court enforcement action and related correspondence, or to requests, suggestions, and recommendations made informally in routine correspondence received by FDA. Routine correspondence does not constitute a petition unless it purports to meet the requirements of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine correspondence will not be treated as a petition and action on such correspondence does not constitute final administrative action subject to judicial review under § 10.45.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dockets Management Staff public list and required entries
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dockets Management Staff will maintain a chronological list of each petition filed under this section and § 10.85 showing: (1) the docket number; (2) the date the petition was filed; (3) the name of the petitioner; (4) the subject matter involved; and (5) the disposition of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency and public tracking of petitions filed under this section (but not petitions submitted elsewhere under § 10.25(a)(1)).
